dossier.public_summary: The 5.37-day dip looks flat and the right duration for a ~2.9 Earth-radius planet, and odd/even and secondary checks are normal. However the measured depth swings by a factor of ~8 between sectors and even within the same TESS pipeline, with two single transits ten times deeper than the rest dominating the detection. That level of inconsistency matches a false alarm from systematics or background blending, not a stable planet, so the signal is best rejected until confirmed by follow-up.

reasons.why: Depth is highly inconsistent between sectors (629 ppm in sector 1 vs 5288 ppm in sector 28 err_ppm 652 and 4787 ppm in sector 68 err_ppm 562) - sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source with p_constant 1.4523729868089548e-11.

Individual transit depths are inconsistent (share_of_top_3 0.942) with two huge outliers at 13093 ppm sigma 8.9 and 12240 ppm sigma 8.6 driving SNR 11.63 from 11 transits, consistent with a few bad events rather than a stable planet.

Flat-bottomed shape and duration ratio 0.9289 (observed_h 1.747 vs central_h 1.881) and size 2.853 Rearth are planet-like, but this is outweighed by the depth variability and outliers which indicate systematic blending/variability; a clean-looking dip alone does not rule out a blended EB false alarm.
No odd/evens difference and secondary snr 2.189 vs best_brightening_snr 3.749 shows no secondary at this period, but does not require a planet when depth changes within the same light-curve product.
